{{Short description|Football club records and statistics}}

This list has details on [[Borussia Dortmund]] records and statistics.

{{TOC limit|3}}

==Head coaches==
In July 1935, Fritz Thelen became the club's first full-time head coach, but was not available in the first months of the season, forcing Dortmund player and [[Germany national football team|Germany]] international [[Ernst Kuzorra]] to take over instead.<ref>{{cite web |title=Die Geschichte des BVB&nbsp;– Teil 4: Die BVB-Historie von 1929 bis 1938 |url=https://www.schwatzgelb.de/2008-02-15-bvb-geschichte-teil4.html |publisher=schwatzgelb.de |access-date=23 July 2013 |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330071851/http://www.schwatzgelb.de/2008-02-15-bvb-geschichte-teil4.html |archive-date=30 March 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Die BVB Trainer-Datenbank |url=https://www.schwatzgelb.de/die_bvb_trainerdatenbank.html&zeige=alle&kat=Name |publisher=schwatzgelb.de |access-date=23 July 2013 |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515084838/http://www.schwatzgelb.de/die_bvb_trainerdatenbank.html%26zeige%3Dalle%26kat%3DName |archive-date=15 May 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1966, [[Willi Multhaup]] led his side to the [[1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]], the first German team to win a European trophy. [[Horst Köppel]] was the coach to bring major silverware to the club for the first time in over 20 years, winning the [[1988–89 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] in 1989.

[[Ottmar Hitzfeld]] is the club's most successful coach, having won both the Bundesliga and [[DFL-Supercup|Supercup]] twice. In [[1996–97 UEFA Champions League|1997]], Dortmund had waited for continental success for over 30 years; Hitzfeld crowned his period with an unexpected triumph and won the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Dortmund won the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] in [[1997 Intercontinental Cup|1997]] and head coach [[Nevio Scala]] became the first and so far the only non-native speaker who won a major title. In [[2001–02 Bundesliga|2001–02]], [[Matthias Sammer]], a former BVB player, brought the league title back to Dortmund. In [[2008–09 Bundesliga|2008–09]], the club approached [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] head coach [[Jürgen Klopp]]. He won the club's seventh championship title in [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11]]. In his [[2011–12 Borussia Dortmund season|fourth season]], Dortmund won the [[2011–12 Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] and the [[2011–12 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] to complete the first league and cup [[Double (association football)|double]] in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dortmund at the Double: history in the making in 2012 |url=https://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/BVB-rewrote-history-in-2012-with-stunning-cup-final-win |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |access-date=27 January 2016 |archive-date=2 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202191959/http://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/BVB-rewrote-history-in-2012-with-stunning-cup-final-win |url-status=live }}</ref>

The current coach is [[Niko Kovač]].<ref>{{cite news |date=30 January 2025 |language=de |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |title=Borussia Dortmund verpflichtet Niko Kovac |url=https://www.bvb.de/de/de/aktuelles/news/news.html/2025/1/30/Borussia-Dortmund-verpflichtet-Niko-Kovac.html |access-date=30 January 2025}}</ref>

==Club captains==
[[File:2023-08-12 TSV Schott Mainz gegen Borussia Dortmund (DFB-Pokal 2023-24) by Sandro Halank–148 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Emre Can]], the current club captain]]
Since 1963, 19 players have held the position of club captain for Borussia Dortmund.<ref name="captains">{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/hummels-zorc-wer-noch-die-bvb-kapitaene-seit-1963-640269/slideshow |title=Hummels, Zorc, wer noch? Die BVB-Kapitäne seit 1963 |publisher=Kicker |language=de |access-date=6 June 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140140/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/startseite/640269/2/slideshow_hummels-zorc-wer-noch-die-bvb-kapitaene-seit-1963.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bvb.de/FAQ/Fragen-zu-einzelnen-Spielern-und-Trainern#faqnav |title=Spieler und Trainer – Wer waren die Mannschaftskapitäne des BVB? |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |language=de |access-date=6 June 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143022/https://www.bvb.de/FAQ/Fragen-zu-einzelnen-Spielern-und-Trainern#faqnav |url-status=live }}</ref> The first club captain after the introduction of the Bundesliga was [[Alfred Schmidt (footballer)|Alfred Schmidt]], who was captain from 1963 to 1965.<ref name="captains"/> The longest-serving captain [[Michael Zorc]], who was club captain from 1988 to 1998, has the distinction of having won the most trophies as captain; he won two [[Bundesliga]] titles, one [[DFB-Pokal]], three [[DFL-Supercup]]s and one [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref name="captains"/> 
The current club captain is [[Emre Can]], who took over after [[Marco Reus]] stepped down from his role as the club's captain for the [[2023–24 Borussia Dortmund season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite news |date=6 July 2023 |language=de |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |title="Fünf Jahre voller Stolz" – Reus tritt als Kapitän zurück |url=https://www.bvb.de/News/Uebersicht/Fuenf-Jahre-voller-Stolz-Reus-tritt-als-Kapitaen-zurueck |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=27 July 2023 |language=de |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |title=Emre Can neuer BVB-Kapitän, Gregor Kobel wird Stellvertreter |url=https://www.bvb.de/News/Uebersicht/Emre-Can-neuer-BVB-Kapitaen-Gregor-Kobel-wird-Stellvertreter/ |access-date=27 July 2023}}</ref>
